affectedPublicSurfaces: NO seller-facing HTTP surface changes. Nothing under `api/routes/` moves, no `/v1/**` or `/demo/**` response shape changes, no prompt, no playbook, no tool registration. This is a CAPTURE slice: its public surface is (a) the contract collection `docs/integrations/tiktok_api/contract-collection.md` and (b) two new guarded client methods on `ProductsResource`. If the executor finds itself editing a route, a ToolSpec or a playbook, the routing was wrong — stop and report.

Contract collection rows added: **A-diag-1** Product Information Issue Diagnosis (`GET /product/202405/products/diagnoses`) and **A-diag-2** Diagnose-and-Optimize (`POST /product/202411/products/diagnose_optimize`), each carrying request (sanitized cURL with `{access_token}`/`{sign}`/`{app_key}` placeholders, exactly as every existing A-row does), the observed response, and the environment line naming SANDBOX_VN shop id `7494751643546977923` / authorization id `7658096633384781588`. A third data row records the Vietnam issue-code list from the listing-quality-diagnosis reference — as DATA in the contract collection, never as prompt text.

`backend/src/juli_backend/integrations/tiktok/constants.py`: two new path constants. `PRODUCT_SEO_API_VERSION = "202405"` already exists (it pins `seo_words`/`suggestions`), so the GET path reuses that pin; the POST needs a NEW version constant for `202411`. Do not retag either existing version pin to make one constant serve both — the versions genuinely differ.

`backend/src/juli_backend/integrations/tiktok/capabilities.py` — the allowlist, and this is the load-bearing surface. `GET /product/202405/products/diagnoses` is NOT matched by the existing `^/product/\d+/products/\d+$` pattern (`diagnoses` is not digits), and `POST /product/202411/products/diagnose_optimize` is not in `PRODUCTION_READ_POST_PATHS`, so BOTH calls are rejected pre-sign today by `ReadOnlyTransportGuard`. The diff adds one exact GET entry (or a `diagnoses`-anchored pattern) plus one POST path, on the production-read side, and the mirrored pair in `SANDBOX_ALLOWED_REQUESTS` so the sandbox capture is reachable at all.

`backend/src/juli_backend/integrations/tiktok/resources/products.py`: two new methods on `ProductsResource` (the class already bound to BOTH `ProductionReadResources` and `SandboxWriteResources` in `factories.py`), so binding is automatic once the methods exist — no factory edit is expected. If a factory edit seems necessary, say why in the PR rather than widening a dataclass silently.

Operator-visible effect: a scope error on the first call is a FACT to record, not a bug to route around. `OP-NFR-1` in the scope report notes no OAuth scope is stored anywhere today, so the runtime cannot pre-check `seller.product.optimize`; the only signal is the vendor's rejection. Record the vendor code and message verbatim in the issue and ask the owner to re-authorise.
Mixed-version hazard: none. No process needs restarting for a capture, because the capture is driven by a test/operator script against the guarded resource, not by `juli-api` or `juli-celery-worker`.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO schema change. Nothing is persisted by this slice: the diagnosis reads are called ad hoc and their responses land in a Markdown reference doc, not in Postgres. rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes: both diagnosis paths stay unreachable (rejected pre-sign by the transport guard, as today), `ProductsResource` keeps its current method set, and Optimize Product stays v2 by S-NFR-10's own rule because its first step is uncaptured. No new exposure, nothing partially applied, no data hazard.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Revert the commit. The rollback is a plain code revert: removing the two client methods and the two allowlist entries returns the guard to today's exact behaviour, and no caller exists yet to break — the methods have zero call sites in this slice by design. The committed contract rows are ADDITIVE documentation; they may be left in place after a code revert (an observed shape stays true), and if they are reverted too nothing in the running system notices. Nothing was written at the vendor, so there is no vendor-side effect a revert fails to undo. Redeploy of the previous release plus a restart of `juli-api` and `juli-celery-worker` is sufficient and no downgrade is required.

doNotInfer: NEVER pass a hand-written example response off as a capture. A row that was not observed is marked 'documented, not captured' in plain words, or it is not committed. B-16's example response (`contract-collection.md` ~line 1409, 'no live sandbox data available at capture time') is exactly the failure this epic exists to end — do not repeat it here.
Do NOT invent the Vietnam issue-code list. It comes from the listing-quality-diagnosis reference; if a code cannot be sourced, record the gap rather than filling it in.

Do NOT widen the allowlist with a loose pattern. `^/product/\d+/products/[^/]+$` would silently admit every unexamined product sub-path; add the two paths exactly (an exact string for the GET, an exact string for the POST) and assert exactness in both directions.

Do NOT touch a production WRITE path. Reads go through `ProductionReadResources`, sandbox calls through `SandboxWriteResources`; the guard must keep refusing every production write path (ADR-068). Never relax `ReadOnlyTransportGuard` to make a call succeed.

Do NOT commit buyer PII. A diagnosis response should carry none, but the redaction rule is unconditional: recipient fields, buyer email, phone and full address are `[REDACTED]` before commit, as every existing A-row does.
Do NOT commit a live token, `sign`, `app_key` or ciphertext. Use the collection's existing `{access_token}` / `{sign}` / `{app_key}` / `{shop_cipher}` placeholders.

If a field ADR-090 d.3 or the spec relies on is ABSENT from the capture, file a documentation-conflict row in PLAN.md §14 with a safe bound. Do not assume it exists, and do not code around it — the design of record is corrected before the dependent workflow lane opens.

A scope error is not a workaround target. If `seller.product.optimize` has not been granted on the connected shop, record the vendor code, ask the owner to re-authorise (a one-minute OAuth click), and retry. Do not degrade, stub, or swap credentials to get a green.

Do NOT add a ToolSpec, a playbook entry, a prompt, or a registry registration. This slice ends at the guarded client method and the committed rows; the Optimize Product lane (#1620) consumes them later.
The Vietnam code list goes into the contract collection as DATA. It must not be pasted into a prompt, a playbook, or copy.
Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051), `apps/`, `ios/`, `packages/`, `docs/product/design/`, or a sibling issue's context cache — this epic's doNotLoad list.
Bind every test collaborator to the REAL object's signature (`TikTokClient.get`, `TikTokClient.post`, `ProductsResource`). A `**kwargs` double proves routing, not that the real call would work.
Do NOT reuse `PRODUCT_API_VERSION` (202309) or retag `PRODUCT_SEO_API_VERSION` for the `202411` POST. Version pins are observed facts, one per endpoint family.
